title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 12-14): Grothendieck sets up the point-set topology of 'conical neighbourhoods' as a step toward the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of stratified spaces. A conical neighbourhood T of a closed subspace Y ⊂ X carries an action I×T→T of the multiplicative monoid I=[0,1]. Its 'boundary' Ṫ is a subspace such that T is the mapping cylinder of a retraction Ṫ→Y. The rescaled pieces are T_λ = λT and Ṫ_λ = λṪ. The 'thickening' Ep_ε(T) = Ṫ ∪ (1-ε)Ṫ-region is ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ.

This page does three things.

(1) A caveat on statement (8) of the previous page. For λ<1, Ṫ_λ = λṪ is the topological frontier of T_λ in X. For λ=1 this fails in general. Counterexample: take X=T itself with Ṫ≠∅. Then the frontier of T in X is empty, but Ṫ is not. This motivates the next page's notion of a 'strict' conical neighbourhood, for which Ṫ is the frontier.

(2) Definition of a 'partie bord' (boundary-type, i.e. collared, closed subset). A closed Y ⊂ X is a partie bord if it has a 'cylindrical' (collar) neighbourhood. Equivalently:
- Y has a conical neighbourhood T whose projection Ṫ→Y is a homeomorphism. Then the mapping cylinder degenerates to Y×I.
- Or: there is a neighbourhood T of Y and a homeomorphism T ≅ Y×I sending y ↦ (y,0) (diagram (10)).
The margin note restates this as a 'voisinage-collier' E ≅ Y×[0,1].

(3) Examples and a stability property.
- For an abstract conical neighbourhood T, Ṫ is a partie bord of T, and likewise Ṫ_λ is one of T_λ.
- Ṫ, (1-ε)Ṫ and their disjoint union are parties bord of Ep_ε(T) ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ, the two ends of a cylinder.
- If X is compact and (Y_i) is a finite family of pairwise disjoint closed subsets, then ∪Y_i is a partie bord iff each Y_i is.

The page serves the next page's proposition. There, T is strict iff Ṫ is a partie bord of X* = X∖T̊, iff T extends outward to T' with T = λT'. This is the collar-extension condition needed to glue strata in the déploiement.
errors: Final claim, 'if' direction: collars of different Y_i may overlap. One must separate the Y_i by disjoint neighbourhoods and shrink each collar to a sub-collar {t ≤ δ(y)}. With X compact (Hausdorff) the Y_i are compact, so normality plus a constant δ from the tube lemma suffices. Compactness is not mentioned in the justification, but the statement as given is correct. The 'only if' direction needs no hypothesis, since the restriction of a collar to the clopen piece Y_i×I is a collar of Y_i.

The equivalence 'conical neighbourhood with Ṫ→Y homeomorphic' ⇔ 'T ≅ Y×I with y↦(y,0)' implicitly uses that T is the mapping cylinder of Ṫ→Y with Y at level 0. This is fine under the (1)-axioms of the previous pages, but the identification Ṫ ↔ Y×{1} should be made explicit.
The cross-reference '(7) devient faux si λ=1' should refer to (8) (the frontier statement), not (7) (Ep_ε ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ).

ideas.what: Conical neighbourhood of a closed subspace, given as a mapping cylinder with an I-action; for λ<1 the level sets λṪ are frontiers, but not for λ=1
ideas.modern_name: mapping-cylinder / conical (tubular) neighbourhood; cf. Siebenmann's locally conelike spaces, Quinn's homotopically stratified sets, Hughes's teardrop neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data, 1970); Siebenmann (1972); Quinn (1988); Hughes (1999-2002)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6, sketches 'déploiement' and tubular neighbourhoods of stratified spaces only informally

ideas.what: 'Partie bord': a closed subset admitting a collar neighbourhood T ≅ Y×I with y↦(y,0)
Ends of a cylinder Ep_ε(T) ≅ [1-ε,1]×Ṫ are collared; a finite disjoint union of closed sets in a compact space is collared iff each piece is
Strictness criterion (prepared here, stated next page): T is strict iff Ṫ is collared on the outside, iff T is a rescaling λT' of a larger conical neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: extendable / proper mapping-cylinder neighbourhood (germ of conical neighbourhoods)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine point-set foundations (collars, frontier caveat) for Grothendieck's stratified-space 'déploiement' programme. The notions are standard (Brown's collars, mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods). Nothing new beyond documenting how he set up the foundations.
transcription_corrections: 'que Ṫ soit la fonction de T dans X' → 'que Ṫ soit la frontière de T dans X'
'(prendre X = T_{Ṫ}, ...)' → '(prendre X = T, pour Ṫ ≠ ∅)'
'partie bonne' / 'sous-espace bon(s)' → 'partie bord' / 'sous-espace(s) bord(s)' (underlined in the manuscript; matches 'partie-bord' on the next page)
'on ce qui revient au même' → 'ou ce qui revient au même'
'un sous-espace bon de T_λ' → likely 'Ṫ_λ est un sous-espace bord de T_λ'
'une partie finie de parties fermées' → 'une famille finie de parties fermées'
The crossed-out 'Bandi' is probably 'Disons' (or 'Disons enfin'), overwritten; the reference '(7)' in line 2 is intended as (8)
